record.title: DEBUG=True reachable in production via non-'True' env spellings — every deploy guard compares raw strings while decouple cast=bool accepts 'true'/'1'/'yes'/'on'
record.description: Three independent gates try to keep DEBUG off in production and all three compare the raw env string, not the parsed boolean: (1) docker/api/entrypoint.sh runs `check --deploy` only `if [ "$DEBUG" != "True" ]`; (2) the CI deploy preflight greps `^DEBUG=True` case-sensitively; (3) every custom security check (DaventProject/checks.py project.E001-E005, envguard E006-E018 prod rules, users.E001-E003) early-returns or is skipped when settings.DEBUG is true. But settings.py parses `DEBUG = config('DEBUG', default=False, cast=bool)` and python-decouple's bool cast uses strtobool semantics (verified by executing the repo venv: 'true','TRUE','1','yes','on','t','y' all -> True). So DEBUG=true/1/yes/TRUE/on in .env or the Render dashboard yields settings.DEBUG=True while the entrypoint still runs check --deploy — which passes vacuously because all project checks return [] under DEBUG and Django's own deploy findings are warnings below --fail-level ERROR — and the CI grep misses it entirely. urls.py then mounts /api/auth/ (api-auth/), /api/schema/, swagger, redoc, and static(MEDIA_URL): the last serves MEDIA_ROOT including private/ chat attachments on deployments without the nginx /media/private/ 404 (Render). Technical 500/404 pages also expose tracebacks. SECURE_* cookie/HSTS defaults flip to insecure under DEBUG, though both documented deploys pin them explicitly via compose/render.yaml env, mitigating that specific downgrade.
record.root_cause: Boolean security gates implemented as exact/case-sensitive shell string comparisons (`[ "$DEBUG" != "True" ]`, `grep '^DEBUG=True'`) instead of comparing the parsed settings.DEBUG, while the settings parser (python-decouple cast=bool -> strtobool) accepts a family of truthy spellings. No check anywhere asserts the effective settings.DEBUG is False in production.
record.intended_behavior: Any env spelling that Django parses as DEBUG=True must be treated identically by the entrypoint gate, the CI preflight, and a system check — production must refuse to boot (or at minimum run a check that can actually fail) whenever the effective DEBUG is true.

grep -q '^DEBUG=True' .env is case-sensitive and misses every other truthy spelling; the Render deploy path has no equivalent gate at all

Local decisive check: Config._cast_boolean -> strtobool; running `DEBUG=<v> python -c config('DEBUG', cast=bool)` printed True for 'true','TRUE','1','yes','on','t','y' and False for '0','no','off','false'

conditions.description: Operator/deploy sets DEBUG to a truthy spelling other than the exact string 'True' in the deploy env (.env on VPS, dashboard env on Render). Not attacker-controlled, but the guard chain exists precisely to catch this class of misconfiguration and all three layers fail on spelling.

On the VPS compose path SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT/SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE/CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE/SECURE_HSTS_* are pinned by x-api-env defaults so the cookie/HSTS downgrade is mitigated there; on Render they are pinned in render.yaml. The schema/docs/api-auth/technical-error-page exposure and (on Render) MEDIA static exposure are unconditional once DEBUG parses True.

execution.attacker_perspective: Not directly attacker-controlled: an operator mistake or compromised deploy config sets DEBUG; afterwards any unauthenticated internet user can reach the exposed surfaces.
instructions: Set DEBUG to a non-'True' truthy spelling in the deploy environment
Restart/redeploy the api service (entrypoint runs check --deploy which returns no errors)
As an anonymous client request /api/schema/, /api/docs/swagger/, /api-auth/ and a non-DRF route that raises to observe the technical debug page; on Render also request /media/private/<known-key>
execution.observed_result: Source + local venv verification: decouple parses all listed spellings to True; entrypoint still runs check --deploy which passes vacuously (all custom checks early-return on settings.DEBUG; Django deploy findings are warnings below --fail-level ERROR); gunicorn boots with settings.DEBUG=True; urls.py DEBUG block mounts schema/docs/browsable API and static(MEDIA_URL).

remediation.strategy: Normalize once and compare the parsed value everywhere: (1) entrypoint.sh and the CI preflight should test settings.DEBUG (e.g. `python -c "import django; django.setup(); from django.conf import settings; raise SystemExit(0 if settings.DEBUG else 1)"`) or grep case-insensitively for all truthy spellings; (2) add an envguard rule that errors when the raw DEBUG env parses truthy in a deploy context; (3) decouple the urls.py DEBUG block from DEBUG alone (require an explicit SCHEMA_ENABLED-style flag) so a DEBUG slip cannot expose schema/docs/media.

code_changes.fixed_code:
if ! python -c "import os,django; os.environ.setdefault('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE','DaventProject.settings'); django.setup(); from django.conf import settings; raise SystemExit(1 if settings.DEBUG else 0)"; then
    if [ "$DEPLOY_CHECK_STRICT" = "1" ]; then
        echo "DEBUG efectivo es True en produccion -> abortando arranque"
        exit 1
    fi
fi
if [ "$DEBUG" != "True" ]; then
    if ! python manage.py check --deploy --fail-level ERROR; then
        ...
    fi
fi

# Replace the case-sensitive grep with a parse-based check:
if grep -iqE '^DEBUG=(true|t|yes|y|on|1)\s*$' .env; then echo "FATAL: DEBUG truthy en el .env de producción"; exit 1; fi

likelihood.reason: Requires an env misconfiguration by the operator or deploy pipeline — not attacker-controlled — but the bypass is deterministic once set and defeats the entire guard chain whose sole purpose is catching exactly this.

impact.reason: Effective DEBUG=True in production exposes the full OpenAPI schema, swagger/redoc, the DRF browsable-API login, technical 500/404 pages with tracebacks, and — on deployments without the nginx /media/private/ 404 (Render, or any no-storage env) — static(MEDIA_URL) serving private/ chat attachments; it also neutralizes every custom deploy check so other misconfigurations pass silently.

confidence.reason: Decouple's bool cast was verified by executing the repo venv (all truthy spellings -> True); every gate (entrypoint.sh:20, ci-cd.yml:480, checks.py:24, users/checks.py:18/38, urls.py:136-145) was re-read in current source.

record.title: StoreSitemap lists stores that fail the public-access gate (missing has_public_link / active-subscription check)
record.description: /sitemap.xml is public and unauthenticated wherever Django serves it. StoreSitemap.items() filters Store.objects only by is_published=True, is_blocked=False, but EVERY public store endpoint (public, public_catalog, pattern/document, contact, reviews, and custom-domain resolve_slug) additionally requires profile_has_benefit(store.user, 'has_public_link'), which resolves through plan_benefits_of -> suscription.grants_access() (active, in-vigencia subscription). is_published defaults True and registration no longer creates a subscription, so any store whose owner never paid / let the plan lapse still appears in the sitemap with its slug and lastmod even though its public page returns 404. The class docstring claims 'las mismas reglas del endpoint publico' — it does not implement them. Caveat verified during validation: the VPS nginx vhost has no /sitemap.xml location (location / falls through to index.html), so on that tier the Django sitemap view is currently unreachable; the leak is live on the Render deploy and any direct-Django serving.
record.root_cause: StoreSitemap.items() replicates only the two boolean flags and omits the subscription-benefit gate that the public viewset enforces per-request.
record.intended_behavior: Sitemap should only list stores whose public URL actually resolves (is_published AND !is_blocked AND owner has has_public_link benefit via active subscription), matching the public endpoint's 404 rule.

trace.description: path('sitemap.xml', sitemap, {'sitemaps': {...StoreSitemap()}}) — public, no auth/throttle
Store.objects.filter(is_published=True, is_blocked=False) — no benefit/subscription filter
public store endpoint raises Http404 unless profile_has_benefit(store.user,'has_public_link') at line 638
benefits {} unless suscription.grants_access() — lapsed/no plan => benefit False => public page 404 but sitemap still lists

evidence.description: items() -> Store.objects.filter(is_published=True, is_blocked=False).only('slug','created_at')
if not profile_has_benefit(store.user, 'has_public_link'): raise Http404
if suscription is not None and suscription.grants_access(): — the subscription gate the sitemap omits
is_published = models.BooleanField(default = True) — unpublished-by-default is not the case; most rows are 'published'
location / { try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html; } with no /sitemap.xml or /robots.txt location — on the VPS nginx tier these Django routes fall through to the SPA (reachability caveat)

conditions.description: Any Store row with is_published=True, is_blocked=False whose owner lacks an active subscription granting has_public_link — the common case since registration no longer creates a subscription.

Reachable wherever Django serves /sitemap.xml directly (Render deploy, dev serverless). On the VPS nginx vhost it currently returns the SPA index.html instead, so exposure there depends on whether/when nginx gains a route for it.

execution.attacker_perspective: Anonymous internet user or search-engine crawler.
instructions: On a deployment where Django serves /sitemap.xml (Render, or VPS if nginx routes it), fetch the sitemap
Compare listed <loc> slugs against GET /api/stores/public/<slug>/ or the SPA store page — lapsed stores 404 but remain listed
execution.observed_result: Source-derived: sitemap <url> entries for slugs that return 404 on the public endpoint; exposes store slugs (business identifiers) and lastmod for tenants that are not actually publicly reachable.

remediation.strategy: Filter StoreSitemap.items() through the same gate as the public endpoint — e.g. restrict to stores whose owner's suscription grants_access() and whose plan enables has_public_link (annotate/exists subquery or a shared queryset helper used by both the sitemap and the public viewset). Optionally also apply the benefit gate to StoreDomain resolve_slug, which has the same omission.

likelihood.reason: Lapsed/unpaid stores are common (registration creates no subscription), but reachability is limited: the VPS nginx tier currently swallows /sitemap.xml into the SPA, leaving the Render/direct-Django path as the live surface.

impact.reason: Unauthenticated enumeration of store slugs (business names) that are not publicly reachable, plus SEO indexing of dead stores; low-sensitivity identifiers only.

confidence.reason: The missing gate is directly visible in sitemaps.py:47-50 versus viewset.py:638 and services.py:54; the nginx reachability caveat was verified in the vhost template.

record.title: RequestIdMiddleware logs raw request.path — percent-encoded control chars forge log lines
record.description: RequestIdMiddleware.__call__ ends every request with logger.info('request id=%s %s %s -> %s (%.0fms)', ..., request.method, request.path, ...). request.path is the URL-decoded PATH_INFO; a request like GET /%0AForged%20log%20entry HTTP/1.1 yields a newline inside the logged path, splitting one access-log record into attacker-shaped lines in stdout (json-file logs on the VPS, Render logs). The incoming X-Request-ID is charset-validated (middleware.py:120-123) but request.path is not, and the ScrubSecretsFilter redacts secret patterns only — it has no control-character stripping (logscrub.py:16-25). nginx proxy_pass forwards the raw request URI and gunicorn unquotes %XX into PATH_INFO per WSGI convention, so the encoded control char survives to Django.
record.root_cause: Untrusted, percent-decoded URL path interpolated into a single-line log record without sanitization/escaping.
record.intended_behavior: Log fields derived from request data should be single-line sanitized (strip/replace [\x00-\x1f\x7f]) before emission.

trace.description: every request passes through; after the response it unconditionally emits the access log line
logger.info('request id=%s %s %s -> %s (%.0fms)', request.request_id, request.method, request.path, ...) — decoded PATH_INFO interpolated unsanitized
patterns redact PEM/JWT/password/path/CUIT only; no control-character stripping, so a decoded %0A/%0D survives into the emitted line

evidence.description: logger.info with request.path as a positional arg
X-Request-ID is validated with re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+') but request.path gets no equivalent treatment
SECRET_PATTERNS contain no [\x00-\x1f\x7f] handling

conditions.description: Any HTTP client can send percent-encoded CR/LF in the path; the WSGI server unquotes PATH_INFO and nginx proxy_pass passes the raw request URI, so the decoded control char reaches Django's request.path.

instructions: Send a request whose path contains percent-encoded control characters
Observe the access log: the decoded newline splits the record and the attacker text appears as a separate log line
execution.observed_result: Source-derived: decoded control characters reach logger.info -> multi-line/forged log records in stdout-collected logs (docker json-file, Render).

remediation.strategy: Sanitize request.path (and method) in RequestIdMiddleware before logging — e.g. re.sub(r'[\x00-\x1f\x7f]', '?', path) — or log request.get_full_path() escaped; alternatively rely on gunicorn accesslog formatting which quotes fields.

likelihood.reason: Trivially triggerable by any client that can reach the API; no preconditions beyond sending an encoded path.

impact.reason: Log/audit integrity only — forged entries can confuse incident review or bury real attacks in noise; no code execution or data exposure.

confidence.reason: The unsanitized interpolation is unambiguous in source; confidence is medium rather than high because end-to-end delivery of a decoded newline depends on standard-but-unverified WSGI/nginx unquoting behavior that could not be exercised live in read-only mode.

record.title: PUBLIC_DOMAIN is unsettable in every deploy path — canonical-host redirects and store-domain CNAME verification are hardcoded to 'davent.com.ar'
record.description: settings.PUBLIC_DOMAIN = config('PUBLIC_DOMAIN', default='davent.com.ar') feeds two mechanisms: (a) CanonicalHostMiddleware builds www.<PUBLIC_DOMAIN> -> <PUBLIC_DOMAIN> 301s (middleware.py:252-263); (b) StoreDomain verification (services/domains.py public_domain()/check_domain/serialize_domain) tells owners to CNAME their custom domain to PUBLIC_DOMAIN and accepts CNAME targets equal to or ending in '.<PUBLIC_DOMAIN>'. PUBLIC_DOMAIN appears nowhere in docker-compose.yml x-api-env (explicit allowlist, lines 22-106), .env.example, or render.yaml envVars — verified by repo-wide grep: only settings.py:36, domains.py:23, middleware.py consume it. So it is ALWAYS 'davent.com.ar' on both deploys regardless of the real platform domain (the repo's own docs disagree: .env.example PLATFORM_DOMAIN=davent.com vs render.yaml davent.com.ar). Depending on the deployed PLATFORM_DOMAIN this produces either: owners following the UI's CNAME instructions pointing traffic at the wrong backend (verified domains that 400 DisallowedHost or serve the other deployment's DB), or — if PLATFORM_DOMAIN=davent.com.ar — an apex->www nginx 301 (default.conf.template:59) fighting Django's www->apex middleware 301 in an infinite loop.
record.claimed_root_cause: PUBLIC_DOMAIN is missing from the compose environment allowlist (x-api-env), .env.example, and render.yaml, so the documented 'env-configurable canonical domain' is unreachable; the hardcoded default 'davent.com.ar' silently wins everywhere — even setting it in .env would not reach the container because compose only injects allowlisted vars.

public_domain() -> settings.PUBLIC_DOMAIN -> CNAME verification target (line 74), UI instructions and tls-ask trust chain (line 124 cname_target)
nginx apex server 301s to www.${PLATFORM_DOMAIN} — opposite canonical direction to Django's www->apex when PUBLIC_DOMAIN coincides with PLATFORM_DOMAIN

envVars block (lines 30-195) contains no PUBLIC_DOMAIN key

blockers: Actual PLATFORM_DOMAIN, PUBLIC_DOMAIN, ALLOWED_HOSTS and FRONTEND_URL values in the VPS .env are not source-visible; PUBLIC_DOMAIN's absence from the allowlist means it cannot be set via compose regardless, but whether the resulting hardcoded 'davent.com.ar' coincides with the live domain determines the impact.
Which deployment(s) actually serve production traffic for davent.com vs davent.com.ar is not source-visible (both compose/VPS and Render blueprint exist).
Whether Render permits dashboard-only env vars not declared in render.yaml (which could still set PUBLIC_DOMAIN there) is a platform behavior, not source-verifiable.

validation_plan.local: Run `docker compose config` with a test .env to confirm PUBLIC_DOMAIN is absent from the rendered api environment; run `python -c` with DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE to print settings.PUBLIC_DOMAIN with the env unset -> 'davent.com.ar'.
validation_plan.deployment: On the VPS: grep '^PLATFORM_DOMAIN\|^PUBLIC_DOMAIN\|^ALLOWED_HOSTS\|^FRONTEND_URL' /opt/davent/.env; curl -sI https://<apex>/ and https://www.<apex>/ observing 301 targets for a loop (apex->www by nginx vs www->apex by Django); in a store-owner session check the 'cname_target' value returned by GET /api/stores/domain/ and whether it matches the platform's real domain. On Render: check the service's environment for a dashboard-set PUBLIC_DOMAIN.

record.title: Django admin unreachable through the VPS web tier for any ADMIN_URL not under /admin/ or /api/ — obfuscation requirement and proxy coverage contradict each other
record.description: The compose/VPS deploy requires ADMIN_URL to be non-predictable: users.E001 fails check --deploy for 'admin/', the CI preflight greps it out (ci-cd.yml:483-487), and DEPLOY_CHECK_STRICT=1 aborts boot. But the nginx vhost (docker/web/templates/default.conf.template) only proxies /api/ (line 107), = /api/token/ (line 112), and literal /admin/ (line 118) to gunicorn; every other path falls to `location / { try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html; }` (lines 158-160) -> SPA. The web container's env only receives PLATFORM_DOMAIN (docker-compose.yml:298-299), so envsubst cannot inject the admin prefix. With the documented pattern ADMIN_URL=gestion-xxx/ (.env.example:28), requests to /gestion-xxx/login/ are answered with index.html — the Django admin is unreachable from the public web entirely (staff would need an SSH tunnel to api:8000, or an ADMIN_URL placed under 'api/' which passes E001 since strip('/')!='admin' but remains guessable). Either the admin is broken-by-deployment — an ops failure that pressures admins to weaken controls — or operators discovered the 'api/' prefix workaround. On Render there is no nginx so admin works at whatever ADMIN_URL is set.
record.claimed_root_cause: nginx location coverage was written for a literal /admin/ path while the security model requires ADMIN_URL to be a non-obvious env path; no nginx location or envsubst variable maps the configured admin prefix to the API upstream, and the web container is never given ADMIN_URL to do so.

settings.ADMIN_URL.strip('/') in ('','admin') -> deploy error; 'admin/' forbidden
ADMIN_URL=gestion-cambiar-por-un-path-aleatorio/ — such a path matches NO nginx location
path(settings.ADMIN_URL, admin.site.urls) — Django side is correct; only the proxy layer lacks the route
web receives only PLATFORM_DOMAIN — the nginx template cannot know ADMIN_URL

evidence.description: location /admin/ is the only admin proxy; no variable-driven admin location exists
location / { try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html; } — any non-/api/, non-/admin/ path returns the SPA
users.E001 forbids ADMIN_URL 'admin'/'admin/'
preflight extracts ADMIN_URL from .env and rejects 'admin'/'admin/' — same constraint
prescribes an obfuscated admin path that matches no nginx location
DEPLOY_CHECK_STRICT=1 -> 'admin/' cannot be used to make the nginx /admin/ location work

blockers: The actual ADMIN_URL in the VPS .env is not source-visible; if it happens to be 'api/<something>/' the admin does work through the /api/ proxy (and 'api/admin/' would satisfy users.E001 while remaining guessable).
Whether staff actually reach the admin via an SSH tunnel or a different mechanism is an ops fact not in the repo.
Whether the VPS or the Render deployment is the live production for staff is not source-visible (Render has no nginx, so admin works there at any ADMIN_URL).

validation_plan.local: Render the nginx template through envsubst with a test PLATFORM_DOMAIN and probe /gestion-x/login/ (expect SPA index.html); alternatively `docker compose config` to confirm web env lacks ADMIN_URL.
validation_plan.deployment: On the VPS: grep '^ADMIN_URL' /opt/davent/.env; curl -sk https://<platform-domain>/<ADMIN_URL>login/ -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{content_type}' — a 200 text/html SPA response instead of the Django admin login confirms the gap; also test an 'api/'-prefixed ADMIN_URL hypothesis if the env shows one.

record.title: Caddy edge image builds caddy-dns/cloudflare plugin at unpinned latest — mutable build input into the TLS terminator for all traffic
record.description: docker/caddy/Dockerfile runs `xcaddy build --with github.com/caddy-dns/cloudflare --replace golang.org/x/net=golang.org/x/net@v0.62.0`. The --replace pins x/net, but the cloudflare plugin module itself has no @version — xcaddy resolves the latest commit of the module repo at image-build time and produces the caddy binary that becomes the production edge: it terminates TLS for the platform wildcard AND on-demand TLS for every verified customer custom domain, holds CF_API_TOKEN (Zone.DNS), and proxies all HTTP. Any writer to that upstream repo (or a compromised module resolution path before sumdb pinning — xcaddy generates a fresh go.mod without a committed go.sum) can land code in the next scheduled/CI image build -> rebuild -> deploy to the edge with full MITM capability over every request including admin sessions and customer PII. Base images caddy:2-builder/caddy:2 are also tag-mutable. Same class, lower trust: compose `docker compose pull` (ci-cd.yml:513) re-pulls tag-mutable postgres:16-alpine and redis:7.4-alpine on every deploy.
record.root_cause: Build input (VCS module + base image tags) not bound to an immutable version/digest; no go.sum committed for the xcaddy module set.
record.intended_behavior: Pin the plugin to a release tag/commit (@vX.Y.Z or pseudo-version), commit the resulting go.mod/go.sum or build via a locked module file, and digest-pin base images (or rely on Dependabot docker updates with review).

postgres:16-alpine (118) and redis:7.4-alpine (142) tag-mutable, re-pulled by `docker compose pull` each deploy (ci-cd.yml:513)

evidence.description: xcaddy build --with github.com/caddy-dns/cloudflare — no version pin on the plugin

conditions.description: A malicious or compromised commit lands in caddy-dns/cloudflare (or its transitive deps) before the next image build, or a mutable base-image tag is repointed; xcaddy generates a fresh go.mod without a committed go.sum so there is no lockfile review surface.
Requires an upstream supply-chain compromise — external trigger, very improbable, but the blast radius is maximal (edge MITM + CF DNS token).

execution.attacker_perspective: Not directly exploitable by a remote attacker; the exposure is a mutable build input into the highest-trust component. A compromised upstream module author or registry path would land code at the next image build.
instructions: (Source review) Confirm the Dockerfile resolves the plugin without a version; confirm Caddyfile routes all platform + customer-domain TLS through the resulting binary
execution.observed_result: Source-confirmed absence of version pin; xcaddy semantics resolve latest by default. Trivy/image scanning would not catch a malicious-but-clean Go module.

remediation.strategy: Pin the plugin: `xcaddy build --with github.com/caddy-dns/cloudflare@v0.5.0` (or current release) and vendor/commit the resulting go.mod+go.sum; digest-pin caddy:2-builder/caddy:2 bases; optionally digest-pin postgres/redis images or accept the risk explicitly.

likelihood.reason: Exploit requires compromise of the upstream caddy-dns/cloudflare repo or repointing of mutable tags — an external, very improbable trigger; the schema has no 'very low' likelihood tier so this is the floor.

impact.reason: Code execution inside the TLS-terminating edge yields full MITM of every platform and verified customer-domain request (admin sessions, customer PII, payment flows) plus possession of CF_API_TOKEN with Zone.DNS scope.

confidence.reason: Dockerfile, Caddyfile and compose/CI pull path all re-read; the absence of any version constraint on --with is unambiguous.
